SKIN. [46] [Chin.]
Excessive, almost painful sensitiveness of skin of whole body, even of palms of hands.
Skin : dry, flaccid ; waxy pale or yellow ; itching, bleeding after scratching ; cold and blue.
The sweat parboils the skin.
Yellow color of skin. θ Jaundice.
Boils on chest ; pimples on loins, arms and chest.
Ulcers ichorous, sensitive ; ichor has a putrid smell.
Ulcers flat, shallow, copious discharge.
Erysipelatous swelling of whole body ; nettlerash coming out after scratching.
Smallpox, pustules black ; variola hemorrhagica, with great exhaustion from copious painful stools.
Psoriasis and ichthyosis.
Pemphigus.
Humid gangrene.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Chin.]
Persons who are highly sensitive to pain, of querulous or discontented disposition.
Suitable to persons of swarthy complexion.
Old women after menopause ; pleurisy, dropsy.
Useful for weakly persons, who have lost much blood or other vital fluids.
Useful for face aches of chlorotic, anemic, leucophlegmatic, scrofulous subjects, and sometimes also in those of arthritic patients.
Child, æt. 2 weeks, prematurely born : jaundice.
Girl, æt. 2, good constitution, lymphatic temperament, diphtheritic laryngitis with night sweat.
Boy with hip disease : profuse suppuration.
Boy, æt. 12 ; intermittent fever.
Girl, æt. 12, suffering some years ; chills and fever.
Young girl, æt. 15, has not menstruated ; hemicrania.
T., æt. 17, weaver, after severe illness four years ago, during which he was frequently bled ; debility and dropsy.
Mrs. M., æt. 20, recently married : intermittent fever.
A blooming girl, now pale and thin ; toothache.
M., strong, slender, blonde ; neuralgic headache after getting wet.
Robust young man ; mania in intermittent.
Young man, pale, cachectic appearance, suffered for ten weeks from quartan ague ; enlarged spleen.
Woman, æt. 23, married one year ; bloody leucorrhœa of five years standing.
Woman, æt. 23, eight days after second confinement ; pleuro-pneumonia.
Woman, æt. 25, slender build, mother of two children ; prosopalgia.
Man, æt. 30, strictly moral ; morbid sexual desire, with morbid craving for dainties.
M. A., æt. 30, periodical cephalalgia.
Hysterical woman ; jaundice.
A thin, weakly woman ; rheumatic ophthalmia during confinement.
A woman in fourth month of pregnancy ; miscarriage.
Woman, after confinement ; ascites.
Lymphatic, scrofulous woman ; rheumatic ophthalmia during lactation.
Woman, æt. 34, phthisical habit ; pneumonia after venesection.
Hannah P., æt. about 35, complexion dark, medium height, had a child five weeks ago, and had for some months past pain in loins ; never had rheumatism ; heart normal ; acute dropsy following parturition.
Woman, æt. 36, blonde, delicate, hysterical ; prosopalgia after massive doses of quinine in cholera.
Woman, æt. 37, small, thin, delicately formed, of a highly nervous organization, mother of several children, operation for strangulated hernia and formation of artificial anus.
Man, æt. 40 ; gonorrhœal iritis.
Man, æt. 40, subject to hemorrhoids ; rheumatism of thigh.
Weakly woman, æt. 40 ; hematemesis after carcinomatous ulcer in stomach.
Woman, æt. 40, nursing tenth child ; hæmoptysis.
Man, æt. 43, blacksmith, tall, dark hair, had phthisis ten years ; hemorrhage from lungs of four weeks duration.
Woman, æt. 45, large, weighing 180 pounds, leucophlegmatic temperament ; intermittent fever.
Woman, æt. 48 ; typhoid fever.
Man, æt. 50 ; amaurosis from sexual excess and alcoholism.
A wiry, intense, active, planning, business man, æt. 50 ; morning diarrhœa.
Two men, one æt. 50, the other 55, both full blooded ; erysipelas of face and hairy portion of head.
Woman, æt. 50, weakly constitution, lively temperament ; menorrhagia.
Woman, æt. 52 ; rheumatism.
Woman, æt. 60, thin and emaciated, subject to gastralgia ; hematemesis.
Married woman, æt. 64 ; biliary calculi.
An old woman, reduced by care and poverty ; pneumonia following intermittent.
Man, æt. 70, retired farmer ; diarrhœa of twenty years standing.
Man, æt. 70 ; nocturnal rheumatism in hip.
Lady, æt. 80 ; coma.
Man, æt. 81 ; painless diarrhœa.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Chin.]
Antidoted by : Aran. diad., Arnica, Arsen. Carb. veg., Eup. perf., Ferrum, Ipec., Laches., Mercur., Natr. mur., Nux vom., Pulsat., Rhus tox., Sepia, Sulphur and Veratr.
It antidotes : Arsen., Calcar., Chamom., Coffea, Ferrum, Helleb., Iodium, Mercur., Sulphur and Veratr.
Is useful in bad effects from excessive tea drinking, and after abuse of Chamomile tea when hemorrhage from uterus results.
Compatible : Calc. phos. (follows well in hydrocephaloid) ; Ferrum.
Incompatible : after Digit. (increases anxiety) ; after Selen.
Complementary : Ferrum.
Compare : Arsen. (great prostration without pain, black stools), Carb. veg. (diarrhœa) ; Coloc. (beer intoxicates easily ; Cedron. (intermittents) ; Cupr. ac. (black, thin, watery stools) ; Pulsat. (bitter taste, etc.) ; Stramon. (black stools) ; Sulphur and Sulph. ac. (sensation as if brain was balancing to and fro and was striking against skull, occasioning pains).
